title: SAS & Quarto
description: ### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. I just wanted to say I've been enjoying using this extension after just downloading it today! I'm not 100% sure if this belongs here, or somewhere else, so please correct me if I'm off base! I see a lot of value in notebooks (Quarto mainly) for SAS/R projects. A lot of students I know use SAS as their faculty mentors know it best. I think the extension really helps make this easier, especially for just running basic `.sas` scripts. I can see how I would teach students to use Quarto/SAS/R together to make nice looking reports and documents for their projects. I've also used `sasquatch` before and had good fun with it, but didn't seem like a lot of features worked with Positron nicely, so I thought I'd just share here. A few things I'm thinking might be useful: 1. With a Quarto document set up according the extension documents, everything runs and the `{sas}` code chunks do indeed route and run through `sasquatch`. One thing that would be really nice is to extend the ability to have the `"Run Cell"` options that the `{r}` code chunks have to the `{sas}` code chunks. 2. In the rendered Quarto documents, there is not any nice highlighting/coloring of the sas code. Am I just missing how to do that? Should there be a better "default" option somewhere? 3. It would be great to be able to send lines of code together through the console like R and Python do in Positron. That way I could just hit `ctrl/cmd + Enter` to send either single or multiline sas code to be executed. I can essentially achieve this by wrapping everything in `sasquatch::sas_run_string()` but that requires the sas code to be wrapped in quotation marks, and you loose the syntax highlighting and other nice functionality. The output does show up in the Plots pane of Positron. Thanks again! title: Clinical Repository upload: send multipart/form-data and don't version uploads by default
description:
### Describe the bug

The Clinical Repository Upload / Upload and Expand commands (PR #67) haven't been verified live yet: the test account has no write permission anywhere, so PR #70 correctly hides them. Comparing the code with the API spec shows two likely problems.

**1. Request format.** `RepositoryModel.upload()` (`client/src/clinical/RepositoryModel.ts`) sends the file as a raw body:

```
PUT /clinicalRepository/repository/items/{containerId}/content?name=…&expand=…[&comment=…][&fileVersion=…]
Content-Type: application/octet-stream
```

This mirrors SAS's own Clinical Acceleration extension. But the CA OpenAPI spec (`putRepositoryItemContent`, developer.sas.com clinicalRepository v3) declares only a `multipart/form-data` body with a single `file` part, plus an optional `filename` field. The viyar notes (sol-eng/viyar#7), verified live on `caf` with an admin account, agree: "multipart, one `file` part. The stored name is the file part's own filename; a separate `filename` form field is ignored."

**2. Uploads are versioned by default.** The upload flow pre-fills the version prompt with `1.0` (ported from SAS's extension), so every upload sends `fileVersion=1.0`. Per the spec, that creates a *versioned* file, and "if versioning is specified, the Enable Versioning and/or Manage Versioning privilege is required". The viyar notes say a normal (non-admin) account lacks those privileges, so uploads could fail with 403 for users who do have write permission.

### Suggested fix

- Send `multipart/form-data` with one `file` part whose filename is the upload's name. Keep `name`, `expand`, `comment` and `fileVersion` as query parameters.
- Leave the version prompt empty by default (an unversioned upload). Only send `fileVersion` when the user enters one (`MAJOR`, `MINOR` or a number such as `2.3`), and accept those values in `validateVersion`.
- Verify both on `caf` with an account that has write access, ideally both with and without the versioning privilege.

### Steps to reproduce

Needs an account with write permission on a Clinical Repository folder:
1. Right-click the folder → Upload…
2. Pick a file and accept the defaults (empty comment, version `1.0`).

### Extension version

v0.3.0

### SAS version

Viya 4 with SAS Clinical Acceleration

description:

- `client/src/connection/stdio/README.md` says SAS starts with `-stdio`; the code passes `-nodms -noterminal -nosyntaxcheck`. It also links `doc/profileExamples/stdio-profile-example.json`; the file is `stdio.json`.
- `package.json` `repository`/`bugs` URLs name `vscode-sas-extension`; the repo is `positron-sas-extension`.
- Docs: `sas9stdio.md` shows an `autoExec` example, but stdio ignores `autoExec`. `additional.md` uses the key `sasPath` (schema: `saspath`). `matrix.md` and its flowchart do not include stdio.

title: Assistant: sas_export_saspy_config writes an IOM-style config for SAS Viya profiles
description:
`profileToSaspyConfig` (`client/src/positron/sasAssistant.ts`) maps a SAS Viya (rest) profile to an IOM-style saspy configuration (`iomhost`, port 8591), with the HTTP access method only as a comment. saspy connects to SAS Viya with the HTTP access method (`url`, `context`, and a token such as `authtoken`).

Expected: a SAS Viya profile exports an HTTP access method configuration.

title: Positron: interrupt on ssh and stdio sessions marks the console idle while SAS keeps running
description:
Only the rest and itc sessions implement `cancel` (`rest/index.ts`, `itc/index.ts`). For ssh and stdio, `interrupt()` in `PositronLanguageRuntimeSession.ts` sets the runtime state back to Idle, but the SAS submission keeps running, so the next submission queues behind it while the console looks idle.

Expected: interrupt the SAS process (for stdio, for example by signalling the child process), or report that interrupt is not supported for this connection type and keep the state Busy.

title: Positron: two SAS consoles of the same connection type share one SAS session
description:
`stdio/index.ts`, `ssh/index.ts` and `rest/index.ts` each return a single shared session object (`getSession` singletons). Two consoles of the same connection type would share one SAS session, and shutting one down closes it for the other (`PositronLanguageRuntimeSession.ts`, shutdown path).

Expected: each console owns its SAS session, or the extension allows only one console per connection type.

Found by code reading; not reproduced yet.

title: Positron: SAS console always connects with the active profile, not the runtime picked
description:
Each `SAS.connectionProfiles` entry appears as a "SAS (<profile>)" runtime, but the session is built from `profileConfig.getActiveProfileDetail()` (`client/src/connection/index.ts`, `getSession()`), not from the profile of the runtime the user picked. Picking "SAS (other)" while a different profile is active connects with the active profile. The code that would switch profiles (`SupervisorAdapter.ts`) is unused because `USE_SUPERVISOR_APPROACH = false` (`client/src/positron/index.ts`).

Expected: starting "SAS (X)" connects with profile X.

Found while documenting the Positron features (code reading, not reproduced yet).

title: Error squiggles from SAS log never appear for code run in the Positron console
description:
### Describe the bug

When SAS code runs through the Positron console, `SASLanguageRuntimeSession.execute()` tries to show log errors and warnings as diagnostics (squiggles, "Fix / Explain with Assistant") in the active SAS editor. It almost certainly never produces any, because the log parser can't find where the submitted code begins in the log.

### Cause

- `execute()` (`client/src/positron/PositronLanguageRuntimeSession.ts`, around line 515) builds a `SASCodeDocument` from the **active editor's whole document**. After the run it calls `sasDiagnostic.updateDiagnostics(executionLogs, codeDoc)` (around line 617).
- `updateDiagnostics` passes `codeDoc.wrappedCodeLineAt(0)` to `parseLog` as the log start flag. That's `/** LOG_START_INDICATOR **/`, added by `SASCodeDocument.insertLogStartIndicator()`.
- `getTheLatestLogs()` in `client/src/components/logViewer/logParser.ts` keeps only the log from the source line equal to that flag onwards. If the flag is never found, it returns `[]`.
- The Positron console never sends that marker. It sends its own wrapper (`options source notes; ods html5(id=vscode) …`) around the console code, not `codeDoc.getWrappedCode()`. So the flag is never in the log, `parseLog` gets no lines, and no diagnostics are produced.

Separately: even with the marker in place, the mapping uses the whole active editor document. Code sent to the console is often a selection, a single statement, or code generated by Positron Assistant, so line and column positions wouldn't line up with the editor anyway.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a SAS session in Positron and open a `.sas` file.
2. Run code containing an error (e.g. `data x; set does.not_exist; run;`) in the console via "Run Selection" or Cmd+Enter.
3. The console shows the error, but no squiggle appears in the editor and nothing appears in the Problems pane.

(Not yet reproduced live; inferred from the code above. Please confirm.)

### Possible fix

- Have `execute()` prepend a log-start marker line to the submitted code and pass it as the flag (e.g. a `parseLog` overload that takes the flag directly). Then map line numbers relative to the submitted code, not the whole document.
- When the code came from an editor selection, offset the mapped lines by the selection's start line. When the code didn't come from the active editor at all (typed in the console, Assistant code), skip editor diagnostics.

Note: PR #66 puts a traceability comment on the first line of each submission without adding a line, so it doesn't change line numbers either way.

### Extension version

v0.2.1 (main at ff6e3e0b)

title: Positron API integration tests against a real Viya server
description:
## Background
The `positron-api` suite added in #36 runs the extension inside a real Positron build, but only for things that don't need SAS (activation and runtime discovery; #61 extends that). Most of the integration only runs once a SAS session is up. We decided to test it against a real Viya server rather than build a fake SAS backend: a fake would only match what we think Viya returns and would drift from the real thing.

The Viya environment is only reachable over Tailscale, so we'll do this in two phases.

## Phase 1: local opt-in suite
- [ ] Add Viya-backed tests (e.g. `client/test/positron-api/viya/`). They are skipped unless the Viya env vars are set, so `npm run test-positron-api` in CI keeps working without them.
- [ ] Configuration from env vars, e.g. `SAS_TEST_VIYA_ENDPOINT`, `SAS_TEST_VIYA_REFRESH_TOKEN` (plus client ID/secret if needed). The tests write a `SAS.connectionProfiles` entry pointing at that endpoint.
- [ ] **Sign-in without a browser.** `positron-test-electron` starts Positron with a fresh temporary user data directory, so an existing Viya sign-in isn't available. Add a hook used only by the tests that seeds the SAS auth session from the refresh token (`client/src/connection/rest/auth.ts` already supports `grant_type=refresh_token`). Put it in files only this fork has, so upstream merges stay clean.
- [ ] A small helper script that gets a refresh token: open the SASLogon authorize URL, paste the code it shows (the built-in `vscode` client displays it), and print the refresh token for the env var.
- [ ] Tests:
  - [ ] Session lifecycle: start the SAS runtime, run code, check the console output, restart, shut down.
  - [ ] Data Connections: browse libraries, tables and Server Files, in both the new pane and the legacy one (`dataConnections.enabled` = false).
  - [ ] Data Explorer: open a table, check the schema and paging, and check the column distributions (#55).
  - [ ] Plots: ODS graphics reach the Plots pane.
- [ ] Test data: a known library or table on the server (or created with a DATA step in WORK at the start of each run). Tests only read, or write to WORK, so runs don't interfere with each other.
- [ ] Document setup and running in `client/test/positron-api/README.md`.

## Phase 2: nightly CI run (later, optional)
- [ ] Join the runner to the tailnet with `tailscale/github-action`, using a Tailscale OAuth client stored as a secret. The runner gets an ephemeral `tag:ci` node, and an ACL lets it reach only the Viya host on port 443.
- [ ] Store the Viya endpoint and refresh token as secrets, and plan for rotating the token when it expires.
- [ ] Trigger on a schedule and on `workflow_dispatch` only, not on pull requests (forks don't get secrets, and Viya runs are slow).
- [ ] Don't use a self-hosted runner inside the tailnet: this repo is public, so pull-request code could end up running inside the private network.

title: Extend Positron API integration tests to the parts that don't need a SAS server
description:
## Background
PR #36 added `client/test/positron-api/`, which runs the extension inside a real Positron build (`npm run test-positron-api`, plus the `positron-api-tests` CI workflow). So far it covers activation and runtime discovery. Several more parts of the integration in `client/src/positron/` can be tested the same way without a SAS server.

## Scope
- [ ] **Data Connections, new pane** (`dataConnections.enabled` true, the 2026.10 default): `isDataConnectionsPaneActive()` returns true and `SasDataConnectionsDriver` is registered through `positron.dataConnections.registerDriver`.
- [ ] **Data Connections, legacy pane** (`dataConnections.enabled` false): the `sas-driver` connection driver is registered through `connections.registerConnectionDriver`. Positron reads this setting only at startup, so this case needs its own launch with a separate user-data or settings directory. This is the path that regressed in #47.
- [ ] **Contributions:** the extension's `SAS.*` commands are registered, the `sas.sas7bdatViewer` custom editor is available, and SAS has its language configuration.
- [ ] **Runtime metadata for each profile type** (Viya, SAS 9 COM, SAS 9 IOM, SSH): runtime name, ID and session location, and the case of a profile with no version.
- [ ] **Local runs on macOS:** `npm run test-positron-api` gets a 403 unless `POSITRON_VERSION` is pinned. `positron-test-electron` 0.0.3 requests `Positron-darwin-2026.10.1-arm64.zip`, but the CDN file is named `Positron-darwin-2026.10.1-2-arm64.zip`, with the build number. CI on Linux works. Report this upstream to posit-dev/positron-test-electron. In the meantime, `tools/run-positron-tests.mjs` could read the version from `releases.json` and pass it through.

## Out of scope
Anything that needs a running SAS session. That will be covered separately by tests against a real Viya server.

title: SAS connection missing from Connections pane on Positron 2026.10 (new Data Connections pane disposes runtime connections)
description:
### Describe the bug

On Positron 2026.10 (build 297) the SAS connection never appears in the Connections pane. Starting a SAS console session (e.g. against SAS Viya) shows no `SAS (<profile>)` entry, and the command `positron.connections.expandAll` reports "command not found".

### Cause

Positron 2026.10 replaces the legacy Connections pane with the new **Data Connections** pane, controlled by the setting `dataConnections.enabled` (default `true`, tagged preview). When that setting is on, the legacy `PositronConnectionsService` no longer attaches runtime connections. Instead it **disposes** every `positron.connection` comm a session opens:

```js
// src/vs/workbench/services/positronConnections/browser/positronConnectionsService.ts
if (configurationService.getValue("dataConnections.enabled") === true) {
  this.runtimeSessionService.onDidStartRuntime((session) => {
    this.closeRuntimeConnections(session); // client.dispose() for every "positron.connection" client
  });
  return;
}
```

The extension exposes SAS libraries exactly that way: `PositronLanguageRuntimeSession.openConnection()` sends a `comm_open` with `target_name: "positron.connection"` and serves `list_objects` / `list_fields` / `preview_object` through `SasConnection` (`client/src/positron/sasConnection.ts`). So the connection is closed as soon as it opens. The legacy view is also hidden, since `positron-connections.connectionsEnabled` is false.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Positron 2026.10.0 (build 297) with default settings, Positron SAS 0.1.0.
2. Sign in to a SAS profile (e.g. Viya) and start a SAS console session.
3. Open the Connections / Data Connections pane: no SAS entry.

### Workaround

Set `"dataConnections.enabled": false` in `settings.json` and **restart** Positron (the value is read once when the service is constructed). The legacy pane comes back and shows the SAS connection.

### Proposed fix

Integrate with the new Data Connections pane via `positron.dataConnections.registerDriver(...)`, the same way the built-in drivers do (`positron-data-driver-sqlite`, `-duckdb`, `-postgresql`, …). Those drivers also use `positron.dataConnections.createDriverLogger(...)` and implement `connect` / `disconnect` / `getChildren` / `getSchema` / `preview`, plus per-language connection code snippets.

Things to sort out:

- **API types:** the bundled `@posit-dev/positron` package (0.2.4) has no `dataConnections` namespace yet. Find the matching typings or proposed API first.
- **Mapping:** SAS libraries map to schemas, members (`DATA`/`VIEW`) to tables/views, and `dictionary.columns` to fields. Reuse `SasClient.getLibraryList` / `getLibraryMembers` / `getDatasetColumns`, and route `preview` to the existing Data Explorer integration.
- **Connection lifecycle:** a SAS "connection" is tied to a running SAS session (profile), not to standalone credentials like a database. Decide whether the driver attaches to the active SAS session or starts one on `connect`.
- **Compatibility:** keep the existing comm-based path for Positron builds without Data Connections, or where `dataConnections.enabled` is `false`, and pick the path at runtime.
- **`PositronConnectionsProvider`:** it uses the legacy `connections.registerConnectionDriver` API and likely needs the same migration.

title: SAS Server view fails on SAS 9.4 remote IOM with the default file root (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'parentFolderUri')`)
description:
### Describe the bug

With a SAS 9.4 (remote - IOM) profile and no `fileNavigationRoot` set (default `USER`), expanding **SAS Server** in the SAS view shows an error notification and an empty tree:

```
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'parentFolderUri')
```

Setting `"fileNavigationRoot": "SYSTEM"` in the same profile makes the view list the server's folders, and Download and Upload work.

### Likely cause

In `client/src/connection/itc/ItcServerAdapter.ts`, `getChildItems` for the root folder runs the `GetChildItems` script for `path: "/"` and then reads `items[0].parentFolderUri` without checking that the list is non-empty:

```ts
const { success, data: items } = await this.execute(ScriptActions.GetChildItems, { path: "/", ...this.fileNavigationRootSettings() });
if (!success) { ...; return []; }
const uri = items[0].parentFolderUri;   // TypeError when items is []
```

With the default `USER` root the call apparently returns `success` with an empty list, so `items[0]` is `undefined`. I did not find out why the list is empty for `USER` on this server (the home folder may be empty or unreadable for the account). Either way, an empty result should not throw; it could return `[]` (or an empty Home node) and log a message.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Windows client with SAS Integration Technologies Client and SAS Providers for OLE DB installed.
2. Profile in `settings.json`:
   ```json
   "SAS.connectionProfiles": { "activeProfile": "iom", "profiles": { "iom": {
     "connectionType": "iom", "host": "<sas-host>", "port": 8591, "username": "<DOMAIN>\\<user>" } } }
   ```
3. Start a session and run any SAS code (it works).
4. Open the SAS view, expand **SAS Server**, enter the password when asked.
5. The error above appears and the tree stays empty.
6. Add `"fileNavigationRoot": "SYSTEM"`, reload the window, sign in again: the tree lists the server's folders.

### Expected behavior

The view lists the user's home folder (the documented default), or shows a clear message when it cannot be read. No unhandled `TypeError`.

### Environment

- Positron 2026.11.1 (user setup) build 4, Code OSS 1.138.0, commit e915bbd8bcb9a26b119ab8fbbec94db5bdf53265
- Extension: posit.positron-sas 1.3.0 (universal)
- OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26100 (Azure Virtual Desktop session)
- Connection: SAS 9.4 remote IOM, port 8591, Windows SAS server, username with domain prefix

### Documentation note

`Features/accessServer` says SAS Server needs SAS Viya in its intro, while a note on the same page lists "SAS 9.4 (remote - IOM)" as supported, and the features matrix marks it supported. It would also help to say on the IOM profile page that `fileNavigationRoot` and `fileNavigationCustomRootPath` apply to IOM (they are documented only on the additional settings page).
